title: Change in Cost of Producing NEWater and Desalinated Water, and Support for Businesses facing New Water Recycling Requirements
what_it_is: Change in Cost of Producing NEWater and Desalinated Water, and Support for Businesses facing New Water Recycling Requirements

sections.label: Rising water production costs
sections.summary: The cost of producing and supplying water has risen substantially since the 2017 price revision.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The cost of producing and supplying water has increased substantially since the last price revision in 2017.

sections.label: Water price increase phases
sections.summary: Water price rises 50 cents per cubic metre over 2024 and 2025, with three-quarters of households seeing under $10 more monthly by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: An increase in water price is thus necessary to catch up with rising costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This is why the Government has announced the revision of water price by 50 cents per cubic metre in two phases, over 2024 and 2025, with a smaller increase in the first phase after due consideration for the current inflationary pressures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With the full increase in water price by 2025, three-quarters of households will see an increase of less than $10 per month in their water bill.

sections.label: Enhanced Water Efficiency Fund
sections.summary: PUB enhanced its Water Efficiency Fund, including a funding cap of up to $5 million for large-scale recycling projects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To better support businesses, PUB has also recently enhanced its Water Efficiency Fund, which businesses can tap on to implement water recycling, adopt innovative technologies for water conservation and conduct studies to identify water-saving opportunities in their operations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This includes an increased funding cap of up to $5 million to support large-scale recycling projects in water-intensive industries.

sections.label: Business utility bill increases
sections.summary: Three-quarters of businesses will see a less than $25 per month utility bill increase from the price revision.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: First, let me also say that in addition to the fact that three-quarters of households will see a less than $10 per month increase in their utility bills without the U-Save rebate by 2025, actually 75% or three-quarters of businesses will also see a less than $25 per month increase in their utility bills as a result of the price revision.

sections.label: Mandatory water recycling requirements
sections.summary: From next year, wafer fabrication plants must meet a minimum 50% water recycling rate, and specific waterwaste streams must be recycled.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In fact, from next year, there will be mandatory water recycling requirements, say, for wafer fabrication plants, a minimum 50% water recycling rate and, for the biomedical and electronics industries, specific waterwaste streams must be recycled.

sections.label: Right pricing of water
sections.summary: Right pricing reflects water's scarcity value, pegging water price to the cost of producing and supplying the next drop.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: When we say "right pricing", we mean we want to reflect the scarcity value of water, that every drop of water is precious and, therefore, the price of water is pegged to the cost of producing and supplying the next drop of water.

sections.label: Households affected by higher tariff
sections.summary: Fewer than 4% of households would be affected by the higher tariff.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The percentage of households that would be affected by this higher tariff is less than 4%.

sections.label: Water price increases
sections.summary: Water prices rose 30% in 2018 and the latest announcement raises them by another 18%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, in 2018, water prices were raised by 30%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The latest announcement by the Government sees them go up by another 18%.

sections.label: Water price review and net income
sections.summary: Water price will be reviewed regularly, and net operating income before grants was negative $109 million in FY2021, widening to negative $264 million.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And we will continue to review our water price regularly, taking into account, of course, costs and other factors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But in FY2021, net operating income, before Government grants, was negative $109 million and it has actually widened to negative $264 million.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: By way of illustration, if you accrue the net income after Government grants for fiscal years 2018 to 2022, it is $1.5 billion.

sections.label: Water-intensive industries and efficiency
sections.summary: Water-intensive industries or large water users do not necessarily use water inefficiently.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: First, let me say that water-intensive industries or large users or consumers of water do not necessarily use water inefficiently.

sections.label: PUB water efficiency measures
sections.summary: PUB works with industries on water efficiency and recycling, mandates 50% minimum recycling for new wafer fabrication projects, and raised the Water Efficiency Fund cap to $5 million.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In addition to that, within each industry, PUB also works with them to look at how we can help them to improve their water efficiency, as well as, where it is possible, to recycle water as much as possible.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: That is why for new projects in wafer fabrication, we are mandating 50% minimum water recycling requirements next year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And for the other industries, we will continue to work with them and see what we can do, in terms of technologies and projects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And that is also the reason why our Water Efficiency Fund funding cap has gone up to $5 million.
